I figured I'd ask y'all how you like to bag cats and get some discussion going just for the hell of it. Here goes:

What's your go-to setup/rig?

I'm using a 7' Medium/Heavy baitcasting rod with a $30 bass pro baitcasting reel, 20lb test mono line with a splitshot to a 1/0 circle hook. Bobber adjusted for depth depending on location for the day.

What bait are you using?

I'm going with hotdog, nightcrawlers, and chicken livers. I want to try live crawfish too, because I hear the big cats love 'em.

Any techniques you use to place your bait?

I don't really do anything more than guess/estimate the depth and toss my bait out to let it sink.

Any tips for a newfag at catfishin'?

Let's hear it, fishergoats.

At the little pond I go to I will take a small green sunfish that I caught, cut it in half, put it on small treble hook, and cast it to the middle of the pond. I use a lead weight like this at the bottom and tie the hook up the line a bit. I make sure my line is pretty tight and just let it sit there while I fish for more sunfish.

If I'm lucky I'll pull out a little bullhead catfish. Not very pretty, but the biggest fish in that pond.

I have not really tried big cat fishing yet, but I recommend this guy: https://www.youtube.com/user/muddyrivercatfishing

I agree with the other comment about Muddy River Catfishing. Another good one is https://www.youtube.com/user/catfishandcarp. Report back if you end up getting a decent sized catfish. I've gone out for them several times, but still only have small ones to show for it.
